name: Patrick Bateman jaw ideal

lead: The Patrick Bateman jaw ideal refers to the practice of citing Bateman from American Psycho, as portrayed by Christian Bale in the 2000 film, as a model for a square, angular, polished look.

Bale reportedly transformed for the role: co-writer Guinevere Turner said he became ripped, very tanned and had his teeth done. Admirers draw on the character's grooming and physique; many viewers read the film itself as satire.

paras: People who reference the ideal focus on controllable parts of the look: leanness and muscle through training, tan, dental work and tidy grooming. Jaw shape itself is mostly bone structure, and forum threads discuss whether it can be developed.
No direct risk attaches to a reference image. Some commentary notes that admiring Bateman as a model overlooks that the character is a murderer in a satirical story.

angle.text: The ideal gives people a concrete picture to aim at for physique and grooming. Jaw structure itself is bone-based, so most steps people take target body composition, teeth and presentation.

lead: Patrick Bateman, the narrator of American Psycho, is a wealthy New York investment banker who leads a secret life as a serial killer. In the 2000 film Christian Bale played him, and director Mary Harron described him as a monster rather than a figure to admire.[1]

Online, some men cite the character as a visual ideal: a lean, muscular, tanned, impeccably groomed man with a square, strong jaw. Harron suggested Bale hit the gym because Bateman exercises, and within two weeks Bale was transformed; Guinevere Turner said he became ripped, very tan, with perfect American teeth.[1]

The film developed a cult following from the mid-2000s and Bateman became a frequent meme subject in the 2010s; some men admire him as a sigma male or symbol of hustle culture, while many viewers read the film as a critique of capitalism.[1]

paras: Bale won the role after auditioning for Harron, who felt other actors treated Bateman as cool while Bale did not. The studio had wanted a bigger star such as Leonardo DiCaprio before hiring Bale.[1]

References to lantern-jawed leading men are long-standing in fitness forums; a 2013 T Nation thread on casting Batman praised a wide, square jaw as essential for the role.[2] A T Nation thread titled around developing a square jaw includes jokes about growing a beard along the intended jaw line.[3]
